correctness.rationale: Cut vertices are forced since omission leaves an entire component beyond reach of a connected dominating set. In the cut-vertex case leaves are optional, with selected leaves deletable. The block-cut tree precludes an outside path joining distinct vertices of a cycle block; a connected selection therefore leaves at most one cyclic omission interval. An interval of length three would leave its middle noncut vertex undominated. The choices empty, singleton or consecutive noncut pair are independent across cycles, and inclusion-minimality takes maximal omissions: all pairs and exactly the singletons isolated within the induced noncut paths, with empty permitted only if there are no noncut vertices. All supersets of a CDS remain connected and dominating, so there is no hidden multivertex-deletion issue. The size enumerator multiplies. Two distinct equal-size pair omissions have symmetric difference two exactly when the free-path edges overlap; singleton omissions form a clique. A pair and an isolated singleton are disjoint and differ in three vertices. Every changed coordinate costs at least two in symmetric difference and the coordinates are disjoint, so a swap changes exactly one coordinate. Components and diameters of the Cartesian product follow. In a bare cycle the maximal omissions are pairs and the exchange graph is the line graph of the cycle (including the triangle); K_1, K_2 and trees give the stated separate cases.
residual_risks: No statement about sharing cycle edges or about reconfiguration allowing temporary size changes. The recorded finite checks do not establish the general theorem.

evidence: The Resultary cactus record allows independent omission of zero, one or two adjacent free vertices on each cycle, with optional leaves. The 2022 theorem provides algorithms for minimal-CDS enumeration including 2-degenerate graphs; the power-domination theorem optimizes a different rule.
broader_coverage.reasoning: Generic enumeration is not itself the exact structural formula. The all-CDS record is materially stronger because it identifies the precise vertex sets of the same graph class coordinate by coordinate.

evidence: The maximal elements among empty, singleton and adjacent-pair omissions are exactly pairs and isolated singleton vertices when noncut vertices exist. A maximal pair is an edge of an induced path in the free-vertex graph; two such pairs are one replacement apart precisely when the edges meet. Isolated singleton choices are pairwise one replacement apart and each is disjoint from every pair.
Independence of blocks and disjoint free-coordinate sets are explicit in the prior characterization.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: There is no additional graph-specific lemma between the prior choice family and the whole Cartesian exchange product: each distinct maximal local choice differs by at least two tokens in symmetric difference, and local adjacency is the clique or path-line-graph calculation. The enumerator and all component and diameter formulas then follow by direct product identities; the bare cycle is the same edge-overlap observation.

evidence: The prior labelled CDS family is a product of optional leaf coordinates and local omissions of size at most two. The frozen vertex family is its minimal antichain, and the replacement graph is the graph of symmetric-difference distance two on that antichain.
Token addition/removal with a size cap is a different graph, even over the same class of inputs.
equivalent_formulations.reasoning: Inclusion reverses to omission on each coordinate, so global minimality is coordinatewise maximality in the already known product. A distance-two edge between antichain choices is exactly a replacement, not a size-changing move.

evidence: The cactus record gives the exact all-CDS product with leaf factor (1+x)^ell, and explicitly identifies the sets counted by each factor. The other record gives an exchange graph on 192 minimum-cardinality CDSs of Q_4.
exact_database_or_table.reasoning: Q_4 is not the cactus case nor the same minimality notion; it is not the reason for rejection. The all-CDS polynomial by itself would not suffice, but its labelled family is an exact dominating description.

originality.rationale: The prior cactus all-CDS result states the full labelled blockwise choice family with independent coordinates, not just a cardinality polynomial. Passing to maximal local omissions gives the exact minimal family and enumerator, and applying the distance-two rule to that product gives the entire asserted exchange graph by elementary direct implication. This is substantive coverage by a stronger result, not an assertion that the prior paper writes the same exchange formula.
residual_risks: No first-publication or priority claim. The conclusion rests on verified implication from a precise known labelled family, not on exhaustive literature search or a claim that any particular paper states the product verbatim.

value.rationale: The exchange question is natural and the formula is convenient, but here it is mechanically implied by the known independent labelled cactus choices: take maximal omissions, then connect local choices by one swap. The component counts and diameters have no additional structural content beyond that product. No scientifically distinct valuable claim survives as a repair of the frozen result.
residual_risks: The judgment is about the claimed advance, not the convenience of writing the known family's reconfiguration consequences for users.
